This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking following reliefs:-
"1.
That, the Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call for the entire records pertaining to the case of the petitioner for kind perusal of Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:28089 this Hon'ble Court.

2. That this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue a writ/writs, direction/
directions, order/ orders to direct the Respondent authorities for determining and disbursing the compensation amount in lieu of her land which are acquired to Respondent Authorities within one month.

3. That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue a writ/writ, order/orders,

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is one of the co-owner of land bearing kh.no.329/2 admeasuring 0.0194 hectare (wrongly mentioned as 0.0240 hectares in para- 8.3 of the writ petition), situated at Village- Sendri, P.H. No.23, Revenue Circle- Koni, District- Bilaspur.
Respondent- NHAI while widening of road has acquired the land situated within the Village- Sendari and other nearby villages through which national highway is passing and have initiated proceedings of land acquisition and thereafter, the Land Acquisition Officer has also passed an award on 01.07.2018.
Some land of the petitioner was forming part of Award, however, land bearing kh. no.329/2 is left out.
The land subject matter of writ petition is Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:28089 also affected with the construction of road.

However, no compensation is calculated and paid to the petitioner and other co-owners and, therefore, aggrieved with arbitrary action on the part of respondents, petitioner submitted representation before the Sub Divisional Officer-cum- Land Acquisition Officer, Bilaspur on 17.02.2023.
However, no steps have been taken.

She also submits that the Halka Patwari has also prepared the list of villagers /farmers whose land is affected and in that list, name of petitioner along with other co-owners is also mentioned showing that petitioner's land comes within certain distance of existing national highway and, therefore,
respondent No.5 be directed to take decision on the pending representation within specified time 3.
Learned counsel for respondents No. 2 & 3 submits that he has filed reply to writ petition.
He submits that petitioner is not entitled for any relief as prayed for.
The land which were affected in construction and widening of National Highway from Bilaspur to Katghora were put to acquisition proceedings.
Notification under Section 3 of the National Highway Act, 1956 was also issued and thereafter the Land Acquisition Officer after computing the amount of compensation has also passed an award.
Answering respondents have deposited the amount of compensation calculated by the Land Acquisition Officer within specified time.
He contended that document which is relied upon by learned counsel for the petitioner as Annexure P-3 is not Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:28089 prepared by the Land Acquisition Officer.
It is appearing that document bears signature of Halka Patwari who, independently, is having no jurisdiction to prepare such type of list without there being any order by the competent authority.
4. Learned counsel for the State also adopts submission of learned counsel for the respondent -NHAI.
He however submits that if representation submitted by the petitioner is pending consideration, it will be considered in accordance with law.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the documents placed on record.

6. Grievance of the petitioner is that petitioner is one of the co- owner of the land bearing kh.no.329/2 and the same is also affected with construction and widening of National Highway Road from Bilaspur to Katghora which is not part of the acquisition proceeding and no Koushalya Bai vs Union Of India on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157837206/
2 compensation is paid to petitioner and other co-owners.

7.

Considering the nature of grievance that the petitioner has not been paid compensation of the affected ownership land , without entering into merits of claim of petitioner, this writ petition at this stage is disposed, directing respondent No.5 to take decision on the application submitted by the petitioner in accordance with Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:28089 law, expeditiously, preferably within a period of 6 months from the date of receipt of order passed by this Court.
